concepts.title: Isolation as Strategic Failure
concepts.description: Machiavelli's objections separated out, and **the sharpest is that a siege does not have to succeed**: the fortress can hold indefinitely and still lose, because a besieged man has stopped doing anything. **The structure converts a defensive success into a strategic defeat**, and no wall thickness addresses it. The crowd's three protections — plotters leak, no single channel to cut, no fixed target — are all properties of **structure, not friendship**, and work among people indifferent to you. ⚠ **Carries the Law 16 contradiction in-page**: Deioces' identical architecture is Law 16's *"ultimate realization."* Also flags that the two losses Greene names differ — your *ear* (you stop hearing) and your *sense of proportion* (you lose the reference class), and the second is what makes isolation self-reinforcing, since a person without proportion treats small threats as large and the standard response to a large threat is to withdraw further

concepts.title: Isolation for Thought
concepts.description: the Reversal, and **the quicksand clause is the real finding**: *"the more isolated you are, the harder it is to break out… without your noticing."* **The cost lands on exit, not during** — so nothing about the experience signals the accumulating debt, and the faculty that would notice is the one being spent. ⚠ Machiavelli did not *choose* isolation, he was exiled after imprisonment, and the case shows involuntary isolation converting fifteen years of prior diplomacy into structure. **Isolation is not generative; it is a converter, and it can only convert what circulation gathered.** ⚠ And the Reversal is **refuted from the margin inside the same law** — Dr Samuel Johnson: *"Solitude is dangerous to reason"* — attacking exactly the faculty the Reversal claims it serves. Eighth instance of the marginal-contradicts-body pattern

concepts.title: The Masque of the Red Death
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Poe, the longest marginal extract in Cluster E, and **it argues a failure mode Law 18 does not have.** Greene's law is about information loss; Poe's fortress fails because **the sealing enclosed the threat**. And the operative decision is not the retreat but the bolts: *"they brought furnaces and massy hammers and welded the bolts… to leave means neither of ingress nor egress to the sudden impulses of despair or of frenzy from within"* — **welded against escape, not entry.** The courtiers were protecting the strategy *from the people executing it*, and **the mechanism that prevents panic also prevents a belief update.** Twelfth marginal text of the build

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster E: Law 17 (5 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 17 COMPLETE, 9 of 9

concepts.title: The Initiative Belongs to Whoever Will Walk Away
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* **the sharpest sentence in the law, spoken by the man who lost.** Spassky before a move was played: *"A man who is willing to commit suicide has the initiative."* Not unpredictability — **credible indifference to the outcome**, a standing property allocated before the contest by how much each party has loaded onto the result. Fischer's forfeited game is **proof of funds**, not pattern-scrambling. ⚠ And the diagnosis was worth nothing: the exposure was a *preference*, the only counter costs the prize, so **the remedy and the loss are the same act.** The asset is not *having alternatives* but *tolerance for the null outcome*, and Spassky's entire Soviet apparatus was in that currency pure liability — **support and exposure are the same substance seen from two angles**

concepts.title: Unpredictability as Terror
concepts.description: the law as stated, and its anthropology: predictability as *animality*, pattern-breaking as the distinctively human capacity. **The target is not primarily frightened, they are working** — the labour is unbounded because there is no pattern to converge on. The cost is *computational*, which is the one asymmetry in the book that favours the underdog by default: **the bigger the machine, the more expensive it is to make it re-plan.** ⚠ Flags that the reason people stay predictable — *they believe if they do not unsettle others they will be left alone* — is dismissed in a clause and is frequently correct

concepts.title: Ali, Foreman and the Announced Strategy
concepts.description: **he told the truth twice and it functioned as the deception.** The announcement, then the loosened ropes — a costly physical signal with a specific technical meaning — and the second was discarded on the *stronger* ground that *"it had to be a setup."* **A prior strong enough to interpret its own counter-evidence is not a belief, it is a trap the holder maintains.** Identical mechanism to Gould at Law 12, uncross-referenced. **Ali's ten-year consistency was not the vulnerability the law names; it was the instrument** — the announcement was unbelievable *because* he was readable

concepts.title: Predictability as a Smoke Screen
concepts.description: the Reversal, and **it identifies the resource the body text tells you to destroy.** Predictability as a *stored asset*: accumulates while you are consistent, spent once on a break. ⚠ Two instruments presented as one, and they are mutually limiting — the smoke screen needs the pattern to hold, the dramatic break destroys it. **Unpredictability buys an exhausted observer watching you closely; predictability buys an unobservant one.** The deciding question the chapter never poses: does your objective require the target *stuck* or *looking elsewhere*

concepts.title: Unpredictability as a Subordinate Liability
concepts.description: the closing warning, which **inverts four pages of recommendation in one paragraph.** Same act: *terror* from above, *"indecisiveness, or even… some more serious psychic problem"* from below. **The operator controls only the act; the reading is assigned by a prior held by other people.** ⚠ The downside is asymmetric and the warning implies it is not — a failed attempt from above is a wasted move, from below it is an acquired reputation, applied retroactively. **Every operator in Law 17 already had standing, and Picasso states the precondition outright**

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster E: Law 16 (4 behavioral-mechanics pages + 1 enrichment, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 16 COMPLETE, 8 of 8

concepts.title: Omnipresence Before Absence
concepts.description: the Reversal, and **one of the good ones: it supplies a criterion.** *"Leave too early and you do not increase your respect, you are simply forgotten… in the beginning, make yourself not scarce but omnipresent."* **Absence has no value of its own — it is a subtraction, worth exactly what was there to remove.** And the threshold is **per-room, not per-career**: what must exist is a reference point in someone else's expectations, not your standing in the world. That reframing explains the failure mode — people below the threshold withdraw, register as zero, and experience it as being undervalued. ⚠ Necessary but not sufficient: it predicts *whether* an effect arrives, not *which*

concepts.title: Death Before Death
concepts.description: withdrawal borrows what death does. **It closes the account** — removing the comparison to a hypothetical better version of you, which is the standard everyone is held to while still present. Charles V's revaluation came from *"people who had hated and feared him"*: the largest open balances release the most, which sentiment cannot explain and this can. ⚠ Every case Greene gives is a **permanent** withdrawal (Charles V died at Yuste, Garbo never returned, Salinger and Pynchon stayed gone) and the technique sold is temporary — the *"air of resurrection"* on return is asserted and never evidenced

concepts.title: The Camel and the Floating Sticks
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* La Fontaine, complete, named and dated. **A working counterexample printed twelve lines from the law's flagship case.** Sentinels shout *"A mighty man-of-war!"* and watch it resolve into a packet boat, a skiff, a bale, and finally sticks. **Same observable curve as Greene's, opposite causation** — nothing was consumed by familiarity, an error the observers invented was corrected. And the two are indistinguishable from inside, so **the law's technique works identically whether or not there is anything behind it** — a failure mode with no error signal. Eleventh marginal fable of the build

concepts.title: The Snow Goose and the Cock
concepts.description: *(re-tiered LOW→MED per the standing marginal-tier finding)* T'ien Jao enumerates the cock's five virtues in full — civility, strength, courage, benevolence, veracity — and then: *"the cock is daily killed to fill a dish on your table… the reason is that it is found within our reach."* **Merit is not discounted by abundance; it is simply not the variable read.** And every one of the five is a *service* virtue, so **the qualities that make you useful to a household are the qualities by which the household consumes you.** Third marginal fable across two laws arguing the subordinate's protection is **exit, not usefulness** — after Kipling's cat and Tolstoy's two horses at Law 11, whose body text argues the reverse

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster E: Law 15 (5 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 15 COMPLETE, 9 of 9 (incl. 1 rebuild in place)

concepts.title: Caress or Annihilate
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* the Machiavelli Authority, and **the strongest single finding in the law**. *"Men must either be caressed or else annihilated"* is a **two-branch rule with a forbidden middle**, and Greene's chapter denies one branch outright, collapsing it into *"never go halfway."* The second half supplies the **threshold the law lacks** — the injury must exceed *the enemy's remaining capacity for vengeance*, which is relative to them rather than absolute. It sorts three of the law's four cases better than the law does, and **it answers Versailles**, which Greene's own Reversal could not: Versailles was the forbidden middle

concepts.title: Clausewitz and the Negotiation Trap
concepts.description: *"Negotiation is the insidious viper that will eat away at your victory."* **The one argument in Law 15 that needs no psychology and survives with all the cruelty removed.** A partial victory does not leave a weakened enemy, it manufactures a *legitimate participant* — and the partial victor then arrives holding more and caring less against someone holding less and caring more. ⚠ Flags that Clausewitz derived the doctrine from Napoleon, whose career is its standing refutation

concepts.title: Banishment, Not Murder
concepts.description: *"It is not, of course, a question of murder, it is a question of banishment"* — arriving after four pages of annihilation language and five cases that are all killings. **Not one of the law's cases is a banishment**, and *"of course"* installs a moral boundary without defending it, at precisely the point a reader would otherwise stop. ⚠ And the fallback when banishment is unavailable is **wariness** — the exact behaviour the chapter calls fatal, and the ordinary condition for nearly every reader

concepts.title: Let Them Destroy Themselves
concepts.description: the Reversal, which **does not reverse**: its stated precondition (*"only when you are sure they have no chance of recovery"*) reinstates the law and merely swaps the instrument. Third such Reversal in the build, after Laws 7 and 14. **A retreat contains no event for the losing side to organise around**, which is why it demoralises more than a defeat. ⚠ Flags the Versailles exchange as argument-shaped without being an argument — an empirical objection answered with *"simply crush them again"*, a form no observation can contradict — and that the operator's feelings switch status mid-chapter, an obstacle when they counsel restraint and a benefit when free

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster E: Law 14 (3 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 14 COMPLETE, 6 of 6 · CLUSTER E OPENS

concepts.title: Talleyrand as Conversational Spy
concepts.description: a documented reputation as the age's finest conversationalist attached to a man who *"actually said very little."* **Suppression is the instrument, not the courtesy before it** — a conversation has fixed air in it, and every sentence you spend on your own view is one they did not spend on theirs. The second method is sharper: *"he would blurt out what seemed to be a secret (actually something he had made up), then watch his listeners' reactions"* — Baron von Stetten, *"Monsieur Talleyrand fires a pistol into the air to see who will jump out the window."* **This inverts the spy's basic problem**: the subject supplies nothing, so nothing passes their filter; the operator supplies the stimulus and reads the involuntary response. Broadcast, unattributable, self-verifying. ⚠ Flags the cost Greene never counts — the invented secret keeps travelling, so the instrument permanently alters what it measures — and that Greene's ranking of self-spying over proxy-spying is refuted by Duveen in the same chapter

concepts.title: The False Confession as Reagent
concepts.description: La Rochefoucauld, *"one is sincere in order to draw out the confidence and secrets of the other,"* and Greene's gloss: *give them a false confession and they will give you a real one.* The marginal Schopenhauer supplies an **inverse pair** — believe the suspected liar so he elaborates past his reserve, disbelieve the suspected concealer so he produces his proof to defeat you. **The sorting variable is whether the person has something true in reserve**, and Greene's summary drops that precondition, converting a targeted diagnostic into general-purpose irritation. ⚠ Prices two costs the chapter omits: a fabricated liability about yourself enters permanent circulation, and being told to your face you are not believed is not refunded by being right

concepts.title: Foreknowledge Has Only One Source
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* the chapter's unstated epistemology, made by **three voices that never meet**: Sun-tzu's Authority rules out spirits, gods, astrology **and analogy with past events**; Greene independently dismisses horoscope and tarot thirty-seven lines earlier; Kautilya's marginal makes spying an *organ* allocated by rank — *"Rulers see through spies, as cows through smell."* **The exclusion of precedent is the aggressive one and it disqualifies Greene's own book**, which is four hundred pages of reasoning by analogy with past events. ⚠ And the doctrine is refuted forty lines later by the V-1 campaign: **Sun-tzu's rule optimises for accuracy and ignores capture**, so the real variable is not source-type but whether a channel can be cross-checked

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster D: Law 13 (3 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 13 COMPLETE · CLUSTER D COMPLETE, 35 of 35

concepts.title: Self-Interest as the Universal Language
concepts.description: *"even the most powerful person is locked inside needs of his own"* — which makes the law about **preoccupation** rather than greed: your urgency does not travel. Carries *"every person you deal with is like another culture"*, the instruction not to be subtle, and the four currencies (vanity, standing, enemies, money) that stop it collapsing into *offer cash*. ⚠ Flags that Ch'u-Ts'ai's access — *"managed to make himself a trusted adviser"* — is the load-bearing precondition and gets three words

concepts.title: The Need to Be Seen Giving
concepts.description: the Reversal. *"They are strong enough to need nothing from you except the chance to feel superior. This is the wine that intoxicates them"* — and **the publicity is the product**, not vanity attached to it. **Its matching rule quietly demotes the whole chapter**: a reader who applies Law 13 uniformly has been trained in the wrong reflex for anyone comfortable enough not to need them. ⚠ If wanting to feel noble counts as self-interest, the law covers everything and constrains nothing

concepts.title: The Peasant and the Apple-Tree
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Aesop, and a cleaner controlled comparison than anything in the body text: both appeals run on the same man about the same tree, minutes apart. **The birds' appeal was heard and answered with two more swings of the axe** — so it failed after being priced, not through inattention. What stopped him was honey nobody advocated for, which means **the winning move is not an appeal at all**. He then called the tree *sacred*: satisfied self-interest converts into sincere value, so the convert never experiences having been bought

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster D: Law 12 (5 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 12 COMPLETE, 8 of 8

concepts.title: Giving Before You Take
concepts.description: the mechanism, and a genuine three-way analysis: **take** creates an enemy with a grievance, **ask** creates resentment at your neediness, **give first** leaves no residue. Carries the operational refinement that *a series of acts — but these can be quite inconsequential* beats one grand gesture, and Greene's own scare quotes around *"honest" admission*. ⚠ Documents that his definition of deception as *distraction* does not fit his own flagship case

concepts.title: Lustig and Al Capone
concepts.description: $50,000 returned to the penny after sixty days in a safe-deposit box, for a $5,000 payoff. **Capone was never deceived** — *"I knew it the moment you walked in here"* — so the mechanism is not installed trust but a broken judgement, and the action happens in the confusion. **Suspicion is an appetite, not armour**: the man surrounded by wolves is starving for one honest gesture and has no calibration for it. ⚠ Flags that the economics are irrational and the epigraph names boredom as the real motive

concepts.title: The Honesty of Dishonesty
concepts.description: the Reversal, and two different techniques under one heading. Lustig saves the Eiffel Tower con by **supplying a worse fact about himself** — the mark relaxes on being asked for a bribe, because a clean official did not fit his model. Talleyrand generates years of purposeless obvious lies so his real ones cannot be found. ⚠ Argues the Reversal is not a reversal: both install a stable classification and operate inside it

concepts.title: The Trojan Horse as Gift
concepts.description: **Neoptolemus's objection is raised, never answered, and settled by a show of hands** among the men who would otherwise do the dying. The gift exemption is social rather than cognitive: refusing a present requires accusing the giver, and that cost is highest where the relationship is most hostile. ⚠ Flags that this is myth narrated in the same register as the Lustig and Gould cases, with no source named

concepts.title: Francesco Borri and the Refusal of Payment
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* took no payment, gave great sums to the poor, received nothing by post, and lived in splendour — so Amsterdam *"presumed that he possessed the philosophers' stone."* **The refusal deleted the ordinary explanation and the audience supplied an extraordinary one.** A persona rather than a gesture: Lustig needs contrast, Borri needs consistency. The prize was never fees but **custody**. Cited to Grete de Francesco, *The Power of the Charlatan* (1939) — the strongest attribution in the law, and it is in the margin

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster D: Law 11 — part 2 (3 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 11 COMPLETE, 12 of 12

concepts.title: Intensive Versus Extensive Dependence
concepts.description: Michelangelo (one irreplaceable skill) against Kissinger (entangled across departments). **The real variable is portability**: intensive power is owned and walks out with you; extensive power is a position with a landlord. Greene's preference is correct and his reason is the whole content — *those who have it depend on no particular master.* Also documents the third architecture he recommends when the first is unavailable — *the appearance of specialized knowledge* — and concedes is weaker

concepts.title: Fear Over Love as the Basis of Dependence
concepts.description: *"fear you can control; love, never."* **The operative phrase is *fear of the consequences of losing you* — fear of a situation, not of a person**, which turns the instruction from *be threatening* into *make the counterfactual legible*. Carries the chapter's near-controlled test: two kings, one courted and one openly hostile, identical outcome. ⚠ Argues the better axis is *live requirement vs backward-facing claim*, which absorbs the condottieri case the fear/love framing cannot

concepts.title: The Secret Intelligence Tactic
concepts.description: the one route Greene introduces and withdraws in the same paragraph. **A secret is a veto, not an instrument**: it cannot be spent without being destroyed, it accumulates one enemy per file, and it produces a master who wants you *gone*. ⚠ Flags that Greene rejects it on grounds of *peace* — a criterion the corpus uses nowhere else — because his framework has no vocabulary for a dependency with the sign reversed

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster D: Law 11 — part 1 (4 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09)

concepts.title: Seek the Weak Master
concepts.description: *"no one will come to depend on you if they are already strong."* **Greene's flagship case refutes the judgment's own rule** — *never teach them enough so that they can do without you* against a Bismarck who restored the monarchy and grew safer. Also documents that *reverse independence* is a tether described as freedom (it requires permanent availability), and that the chapter's Machiavelli epigraph runs the identical law from *above*, making it the law's own undeclared countermeasure

concepts.title: The Cat That Walked by Himself
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Kipling. A place by the fire and milk three times a day, mice and kindness to babies in return, a stated breach clause about the tail, and *"all places are alike to him."* **Bounded dependence with full autonomy — printed twelve lines from Greene's claim that the best you can hope for is reverse independence.** Bismarck's security came from being expensive to lose; the cat's comes from being cheap to keep, and only one of those is available to someone ordinary. Prices its own cost honestly: three men in five throw things at him

concepts.title: The Vine and the Elm
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Dodsley. **The support she refused was free** — the elm asked nothing and had already offered. She declined a costless deal and then spent real resources advertising the refusal: *"to support for a moment their empty boast of independence, have exhausted the very source of it."* The display and the capacity draw on the same juices. What ruins her is not independence but the audience for it. ⚠ Source heading OCR-corrupted

concepts.title: The Two Horses
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Tolstoy. Shedding the load worked exactly as intended, and that is what killed him: **the transfer was a public experiment proving one horse could do the whole job**, and the tavern owner simply read the result. Reducing what you carry and demonstrating you are unnecessary are the same act seen from two viewpoints, and only one viewpoint makes the decision

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster D: Law 10 (4 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-09) — ⚠ LAW 10 COMPLETE, 8 of 8

concepts.title: Quarantine, Not Rescue
concepts.description: *"Most important of all, do not take pity."* **Pity does not cause identification, so why forbid the feeling?** Because pity reliably argues for the proportionate response, and this law has only the total one in stock — the prohibition exists to protect the size of the intervention. ⚠ Documents that Greene's exemption for the genuinely unlucky is unusable by his own effects-over-reasons method, and that the sorting criterion the corpus actually runs on is extractable usefulness: Law 2 keeps an assassin, Law 10 excises a depressive

concepts.title: Infection as a Weapon
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Musashi: *"Make a show of complete calmness… You infect their spirit… with a carefree, drunklike spirit, with boredom, or even weakness."* **The offensive form of the law, printed in the margin of a chapter that declares itself to have no reversal.** It also invalidates the diagnostic — a competent transmitter has a clean record and a stable career precisely because it is a tactic rather than a condition. Supplies the mechanism Law 8 never gives for why staying back frustrates an opponent

concepts.title: The Nut and the Campanile Wall
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Leonardo's fable. The nut appeals *"by the grace of God,"* praises the bells, asks for a little hole; the wall is *"moved with compassion"*; the roots prise the stones apart. **It scores zero on all five of Greene's diagnostic signs and destroys the wall completely.** The aperture is not a weakness for intensity but the willingness to shelter — and the wall's compassion was *correct*, which is a harder claim than the chapter's

concepts.title: The Healthy as Prescription
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* Montaigne prescribed as medicine to a rich old consumptive, his countenance and vigour itemised like active ingredients: *"He forgot to add that mine might get worse."* **The only passage in the law written from the position of the person being spent**, and the doctor's prescription is sound medicine on Greene's own premises — the error is that the person being prescribed is not in the model. ⚠ Notes that Greene's positive-infection advice is written entirely from the absorber's chair and is self-limiting at scale

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster C: Law 9 (3 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-08) — ⚠ CLUSTER C COMPLETE

concepts.title: The Arguer
concepts.description: the type built from the Athenian engineer: words are never neutral, so arguing upward impugns a more powerful person's intelligence, and **being right is the accelerant rather than the mitigation** — a less capable man would have run out of diagrams. Carries Greene's rarely-noticed closing criterion (*if time and their own experience will make them understand, don't bother with a demonstration either*), and the finding that the engineer's fatal act was a **demonstration attempted at the wrong end of the sequence**

concepts.title: The Sultan and the Vizier
concepts.description: ten days feeding the sultan's hunting dogs, bought with a hundred gold pieces, then one sentence: *ten days produced this, thirty years produced a death sentence.* **The proof was staged before the argument existed and the sultan asked the question himself** — the demonstration created the permission. ⚠ Flags that the dogs are a *proxy* proving nothing about thirty years, and persuade completely anyway. Folds in the God-and-Abraham passage from the same thirteenth-century Arabic source

concepts.title: Argument as Cover for Deception
concepts.description: the Reversal, and **it refutes the law on its own page**: Sheriff Richards arrived with a gun and a demonstrated proof (a box that visibly did not work) and was argued out of it in under an hour. Argument repurposed from persuasion tool to attention sink, where its uselessness is the feature; phase two is *technical gobbledygook*, which converts the mark's certainty into doubt about himself. ⚠ Notes plainly that the refund was counterfeit and the victim went to prison for passing it

title: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power — PAGE-MAX RE-INGEST, Cluster C: Law 8 (4 behavioral-mechanics pages, 2026-08-08)

concepts.title: Aggression as Loss of Control
concepts.description: the diagnosis, and why a person can be winning continuously while directing nothing: he reacts to enemies *and* to the unforeseen consequences of his own earlier moves, so a sufficiently aggressive operator generates his own workload. Carries Zhang Yu's emptiness/fullness Authority, and the finding that the chapter's emotional-mastery advice is a **positional good** — its value comes entirely from other people lacking it

concepts.title: The Fast Attack Reversal
concepts.description: *"if you have time on your side, and know that you and your enemies are at least at equal strength…"* The criterion has two variables and therefore four quadrants; Greene addresses the two comfortable ones and is silent on **stronger enemy, time against you** — the position most readers are in. Also: both halves of the law buy the same good, initiative, which means the law was never about patience

concepts.title: The Beware of Pickpockets Sign
concepts.description: the most efficient attack in the chapter is a **true warning**. Every word is accurate and heeding it is correct behaviour; the exploit is that protecting something requires locating it, and locating it is visible. Thieves posting their own signs are not defeating a security measure but manufacturing one. ⚠ Flags that this class of attack bypasses the emotions entirely, which is the only vulnerability Greene's defensive apparatus addresses

concepts.title: Fighting on Your Own Territory
concepts.description: two sentences, no case of its own, and the highest ratio of usefulness to word count in the law. The reliable half is not the visitor's nervousness but the host's **spare attentional capacity**; and Greene's subordinate clause *"or the territory of your choice"* is the better version, because chosen third ground reads as neutral and isn't

concepts.title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants
